research.summary: For a sideloaded Kotlin/Compose interval timer on a Galaxy Z Flip 7 (Android 16 / API 36, One UI 8): a started+bound foreground service of type specialUse owns the clock and exposes an immutable StateFlow the Compose UI collects; timing is anchored to absolute SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() targets (never accumulated postDelayed/delay deltas), so remaining time is recomputed every tick and survives lock/unlock, Activity recreation, and display switches. The single most important correctness fact: a foreground service does NOT keep the CPU awake — you must hold a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK for the running workout so per-second beeps land on time while the screen is off. specialUse is the right FGS type (no runtime timeout, only the FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE permission, no sensor permissions, Play subtype review irrelevant for a sideloaded APK). The only real threat to on-time beeps is deep Doze, which explicitly ignores wake locks; mitigate by prompting the user to exempt the app from battery optimization. No AlarmManager/exact alarms are needed for the running timer. Keep the screen on in-foreground with FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON.

findings.title: Target is Android 16 / API level 36 — set compileSdk/targetSdk 36
findings.detail: The Galaxy Z Flip 7 ships with Android 16 and One UI 8 out of the box. Android 16 is API level 36. Because the spec targets a single newest device, compileSdk = targetSdk = 36 and minSdk can be 36 (34 is the floor for the mandatory FGS-type APIs). Android 16's Live Updates API (surfaced as One UI 8's Now Bar on the FlexWindow cover screen) is the mechanism that can promote the timer's ongoing notification onto the cover screen.

findings.title: (1) Drift-free timing: anchor to SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() absolute targets, never accumulate deltas
findings.detail: Compute each interval's end as endTarget = startElapsed + durationMs where startElapsed = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime(), and every tick derive remaining = endTarget minus SystemClock.elapsedRealtime(). elapsedRealtime() is monotonic and, critically, INCLUDES deep sleep, so remaining time is always correct even if the CPU napped. Do NOT accumulate Handler.postDelayed/coroutine delay deltas: postDelayed schedules against SystemClock.uptimeMillis(), which STOPS during deep sleep, and accumulation compounds jitter into drift. elapsedRealtime is the recommended basis for interval timing. On pause store remaining = endTarget minus now; on resume set endTarget = now + remaining — keeps timing exact across pauses.

findings.title: (1b) Sub-second beep cues landing on the second: precompute cue targets, delay-then-recompute-and-fire, preload the audio
findings.detail: Precompute an ordered list of absolute cue timestamps for the lead-in and each transition (cueTarget = intervalEnd minus 5000/3000/2000/1000/0 ms). Timing loop: read now = elapsedRealtime(); delay(nextCue minus now), then on wake recompute now and fire the beep once now has reached cueTarget (fire immediately if the sleep overshot). Because you re-anchor to elapsedRealtime after every wake, a few-ms scheduler jitter never accumulates. Keep the audible onset tight by pre-loading the distinct 5s tone, the 3/2/1 short beeps, and the go tone into a SoundPool (or a warm AudioTrack) at workout start so play() latency is a fixed small offset rather than a load stall; to place the sound's onset exactly on the second, subtract a measured constant output-latency offset from the scheduled delay. (Music-ducking via AudioManager audio focus AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK is really the audio dimension but hangs off this same per-beep code path.)

findings.title: (2) Foreground service type: use specialUse — no timeout, minimal permissions, Play subtype review moot for a sideloaded APK
findings.detail: Declare android:foregroundServiceType=specialUse with the required property element (android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE, value e.g. interval_timer_countdown_cues) inside the service element. Manifest permissions: FOREGROUND_SERVICE plus FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE. specialUse has NO runtime timeout and requires NO extra runtime permissions (unlike health, which needs FOREGROUND_SERVICE_HEALTH plus a sensor/ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION permission). Avoid dataSync and mediaProcessing — both capped (dataSync time-limited on API 35+, mediaProcessing 6h/24h). mediaPlayback is the only other no-timeout candidate and is technically defensible (the app does play audio) but is semantically for continuous media with a MediaSession and pulls in FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK plus media-session expectations you don't need. For a beep-only timer, specialUse is the lazy correct fit. The subtype string is only reviewed at Google Play submission — irrelevant for a sideloaded APK — but the property element must still be present because the platform reads it. Since Android 14 (API 34), omitting the type-specific permission throws SecurityException at startForeground().

findings.title: (2b) Mandatory notification + POST_NOTIFICATIONS — service runs even if the permission is denied
findings.detail: A foreground service must post an ongoing notification (create a low-importance channel; that ongoing notification is where the cover-screen Live Update/Now Bar can surface). POST_NOTIFICATIONS is a runtime permission since Android 13 (API 33) and you should request it. Key behavior: you do NOT need POST_NOTIFICATIONS to launch the FGS, and if the user DENIES it the service STILL runs and keeps beeping — only the drawer notification is hidden (it still appears in the FGS Task Manager). Start the FGS from the user's Start tap (app visible/foreground), always permitted, sidestepping background-start restrictions; call startForeground() promptly (within the platform's few-second window) to avoid an ANR/RemoteServiceException.

findings.title: (2c/CRITICAL) A foreground service does NOT keep the CPU awake — hold a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK so beeps fire with the screen off
findings.detail: Make-or-break fact. An FGS prevents process death and background-start restrictions but does NOT keep the CPU running; when the screen turns off the CPU can suspend and the coroutine/Handler timing loop freezes, so per-second beeps arrive late or not until the next wake. To keep sub-second cues landing while the screen is off/backgrounded, the service must acquire a PowerManager.PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK for the duration of the running workout (permission android.permission.WAKE_LOCK, a normal permission, no prompt). API: powerManager.newWakeLock(PowerManager.PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK, tag), acquire(safetyTimeoutMs), release() on pause/stop/onDestroy. Use the timeout overload as a safety cap so a crash can't leave it stuck; release whenever paused or the workout ends. A partial wake lock keeps the CPU on with the screen off — exactly what running/interval apps do. FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON does NOT substitute: it only holds while a visible Activity is foreground.

findings.title: (2d) Doze is the one thing that beats the wake lock — mitigate with a battery-optimization exemption
findings.detail: Doze mode explicitly ignores wake locks and defers standard alarms/jobs. It activates when the device is unplugged, stationary (no motion), and screen-off for an extended period. During an ACTIVE workout this is usually not reached: intervals are seconds long, the phone is often handled/moving (stationarity check fails), and the FGS keeps the app alive. The realistic risk is a long screen-off rest with the phone flat and still, long enough for deep Doze, after which the CPU can sleep and the final countdown beeps slip. Mitigations, best first: (a) prompt once to exempt the app from battery optimization — PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(pkg) plus Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS (permission REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS); whitelisted apps keep wake locks/alarms honored under Doze. Play restricts that permission but this APK is sideloaded. (b) As belt-and-braces, schedule one AlarmManager.setExactAndAllowWhileIdle() at intervalEnd minus roughly 6s to wake the device and re-acquire the wake lock before the final beeps — capped once per 9 minutes under Doze, so it can wake for the final countdown but cannot drive per-second beeps.

findings.title: (3) Keep the screen ON in foreground: FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON (Activity-only, no permission), wired via a Compose DisposableEffect
findings.detail: Use window.addFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON) / clearFlags(...) (equivalent to the android:keepScreenOn view attribute). No permission required. In Compose, wrap it in a DisposableEffect on the timer screen that adds the flag on enter and clears it on dispose (or set LocalView.current.keepScreenOn = true for the composable's lifetime). Limits: the flag only works while set on a visible Activity — nothing in a Service, and the system lets the screen turn off normally once backgrounded. It keeps the display (and CPU) up only while the timer UI is foreground; it is NOT a substitute for the partial wake lock that covers screen-off/backgrounded. Prefer the flag over a screen-bright wake lock because it is scoped to the Activity and auto-clears. Clean split: FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON = screen while looking at it; PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK = beeps while screen is off.

findings.title: (4) Architecture: the FGS owns the clock and publishes an immutable StateFlow; Compose only collects it
findings.detail: Run a started plus bound foreground service (startForegroundService() then bindService()), or expose state from a process-level singleton/repository the service writes and the UI reads. The service holds all authoritative timing state (current interval index, phase Work/Rest, endTargetElapsed, isPaused, pausedRemaining) and runs a coroutine on its own scope ticking roughly every 16 to 50 ms, emitting an immutable data class TimerUiState through a MutableStateFlow. Compose collects via collectAsStateWithLifecycle(). Because every value is DERIVED from elapsedRealtime() against targets stored in the service — not from UI-thread accumulators — Activity recreation (fold/unfold, rotation, moving to the FlexWindow, config changes) never disturbs timing: the recreated Activity simply re-binds/re-collects the same StateFlow and paints the current remaining value. Pause/Resume are pure state transitions on the service. This satisfies lock/unlock or a display switch never disrupts timing by construction.

findings.title: (5) Android 14/15/16 FGS + exact-alarm restrictions — none block a specialUse timer, and no exact alarm is needed
findings.detail: Android 14 (API 34): FGS types mandatory; must hold FOREGROUND_SERVICE plus the type-specific permission or startForeground() throws SecurityException. Android 15 (API 35): runtime timeouts added for dataSync and mediaProcessing (NOT specialUse/mediaPlayback/health); BOOT_COMPLETED receivers can no longer start certain FGS types — irrelevant since you start from the user's tap. Android 16 (API 36): background jobs started from an FGS are subject to JobScheduler/WorkManager quotas (you use no jobs), and background activity/FGS starts are further hardened (you start from a visible Activity, always allowed). Net: a specialUse FGS started from the foreground has no timeout and no new blocker on API 36. On exact alarms: you do NOT need AlarmManager for the running timer — the wake lock plus coroutine loop drives all cues; use setExactAndAllowWhileIdle only as the optional Doze wake-trigger. SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is denied-by-default since Android 13/14 (check canScheduleExactAlarms()); USE_EXACT_ALARM is reserved for alarm-clock/calendar apps — another reason to avoid the alarm path for the normal flow.

findings.title: Cover-screen (FlexWindow) via Good Lock MultiStar — service-owned clock makes the display switch safe, but MultiStar itself is unverifiable in AOSP docs
findings.detail: Moving an Activity between the inner display and the 4.1-inch FlexWindow is a display/configuration change that can recreate the Activity; because the clock lives in the service, recreation does not disrupt timing (the new Activity re-collects the StateFlow). Running an arbitrary sideloaded app on the cover screen comes from Samsung's Good Lock MultiStar (apps on cover screen) module — a One UI feature, not standard AOSP — so its exact Activity-lifecycle and window-inset behavior (including keeping the bottom-corner camera cutout clear) cannot be verified against official Android docs and must be tested on-device. Design the cover layout with WindowInsets/safe-area padding and treat MultiStar behavior as device-specific.

recommendations: FGS type = specialUse. Manifest: uses-permission FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE, WAKE_LOCK, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS; service android:foregroundServiceType=specialUse with the PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE property element present.

Put the clock in the service. Store absolute endTargetElapsed from SystemClock.elapsedRealtime(); every tick compute remaining = target minus now; publish an immutable StateFlow the Compose UI collects with collectAsStateWithLifecycle(). Never accumulate postDelayed/delay deltas.
Acquire a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK while the timer is RUNNING (release on pause/end/onDestroy, acquire with a safety timeout) — this, not the FGS, is what makes screen-off beeps land on the second.

Beep scheduling loop: precompute cue timestamps (lead-in plus each transition at 5/3/2/1/0 s before the boundary), delay to the next, then recompute-and-fire on wake so jitter never accumulates. Preload all tones in SoundPool at workout start.
Keep the screen on in-foreground with FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON added/cleared in a Compose DisposableEffect on the timer screen; do not rely on it for the backgrounded case.

On first run, prompt POST_NOTIFICATIONS (ongoing notification / cover-screen Now Bar) and prompt the battery-optimization exemption (ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS) — the exemption is the real fix for Doze eating beeps on long screen-off rests.
Skip AlarmManager for the normal flow. Only add one setExactAndAllowWhileIdle wake-trigger before the final countdown if device testing shows long rests slipping under Doze.
compileSdk/targetSdk = 36; minSdk 36 (34 floor for FGS-type APIs). Start the FGS from the user's Start tap (foreground) to avoid every background-start restriction.
gotchas: A foreground service alone does NOT keep the CPU awake — without a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK, screen-off beeps freeze until the next wake. Most common wrong assumption.

Doze explicitly IGNORES wake locks (not just defers them). Only a battery-optimization exemption (or setExactAndAllowWhileIdle, capped once per 9 minutes) survives deep Doze. Samsung One UI adds aggressive Sleeping apps killing on top of AOSP Doze — expect to manually whitelist the app on-device.

Handler.postDelayed and most delay()/Thread.sleep timing run on the uptimeMillis clock, which STOPS in deep sleep — accumulating their deltas produces silent drift. Always recompute from elapsedRealtime.
FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON only works while set on a visible foreground Activity and can only be set from an Activity — cleared/ineffective once backgrounded, cannot be set from the service.
If the user denies POST_NOTIFICATIONS the service keeps running but its notification is hidden from the drawer (still visible in the FGS Task Manager) — don't treat denial as fatal.
The specialUse property subtype element must be present in the manifest even though its free-form text is only reviewed by Google Play (not applicable to a sideloaded APK).
openQuestions: Does deep Doze realistically trigger mid-workout on the Flip 7 under One UI 8 (Samsung battery management is more aggressive than stock AOSP)? Verify on-device whether the partial wake lock alone holds beeps through a multi-minute screen-off rest, or whether the battery-optimization exemption is mandatory.

How does Good Lock MultiStar drive the Activity lifecycle when the app is shown on / removed from the FlexWindow, and does it recreate the Activity on each fold/unfold? Not documented in AOSP — measure on-device and validate the service-owned-clock assumption against it.

Is coroutine delay() jitter tight enough for perceptually on-the-second beeps, or should the tick run on a Choreographer/high-rate Handler? Measure actual audible-onset error on the Flip 7 (including SoundPool output latency) and calibrate the constant lead offset.

confirmedHighlights: Central claim verified: a foreground service does NOT keep the CPU awake; a PowerManager.PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK is required so per-second beeps land with the screen off. developer.android.com's 'Choose the right API to keep the device awake' explicitly asks whether the device suspending mid-service would hurt UX and, if so, says 'you might need to use a wake lock' — confirming the FGS alone does not hold the CPU. (https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/awake)

Doze behavior is correct: while in deep Doze the system 'ignores wake locks' and defers standard alarms; setAndAllowWhileIdle/setExactAndAllowWhileIdle fire at most once per 9 minutes per app; battery-optimization-exempt apps may 'hold partial wake locks during Doze.' (https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby)

FGS type facts correct: specialUse has NO runtime timeout and requires only FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE plus the mandatory android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE <property> element in the manifest; dataSync and mediaProcessing are the timeout-capped types (6h/24h on API 35+), which the JSON correctly steers away from. (https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/service-types , https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15)

Hardware/SDK correct: Galaxy Z Flip 7 ships with Android 16 and One UI 8, with a 4.1-inch (1048x948) FlexWindow cover screen; Android 16 = API 36, so compileSdk/targetSdk 36 is right. (https://news.samsung.com/us/samsung-galaxy-z-flip7-a-pocket-sized-ai-powerhouse-with-a-new-edge-to-edge-flexwindow/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Z_Flip_7)

Timing model correct: SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() counts deep sleep and is the documented 'recommended basis for interval timing'; uptimeMillis() (Handler/postDelayed) does not advance in deep sleep, so anchoring to absolute elapsedRealtime targets and recomputing each tick is the right drift-free design. (https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/SystemClock)

Exact-alarm facts correct: SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is denied-by-default on Android 14 for apps targeting API 33+ (check canScheduleExactAlarms()), and USE_EXACT_ALARM is reserved for alarm-clock/calendar apps — so avoiding the alarm path for the normal timer flow is sound. (https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/schedule-exact-alarms)

Android 16 Live Updates is real: Notification.ProgressStyle (API 36+) creates progress-centric notifications that can be promoted to appear prominently on system surfaces. (https://developer.android.com/about/versions/16/features/progress-centric-notifications)

issues.claim: Finding 1 (marked high confidence): "Android 16's Live Updates API (surfaced as One UI 8's Now Bar on the FlexWindow cover screen) is the mechanism that can promote the timer's ongoing notification onto the cover screen."
issues.problem: The Android 16 Live Updates API (Notification.ProgressStyle promoted notifications) is real and documented, but that it renders on the Flip 7's FlexWindow via One UI 8's Now Bar is a Samsung-specific, undocumented coupling. The JSON's own cover-screen finding (correctly marked low confidence) admits this behavior 'cannot be verified against official Android docs.' Asserting the same chain at high confidence in Finding 1 is an internal contradiction and over-states certainty.
issues.correction: Only the Android-documented half is verifiable: promoted Live Update notifications appear on system surfaces (drawer top, lock screen, status-bar chip). Whether One UI 8's Now Bar renders them on the FlexWindow must be tested on-device; downgrade Finding 1's confidence to match the cover-screen finding and treat cover-screen promotion as device-specific/untested.

issues.claim: UI guidance covers FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON via a Compose DisposableEffect and WindowInsets/safe-area padding for the cover screen, but says nothing about Android 16's edge-to-edge enforcement.
issues.problem: Omission that directly affects this build. Apps targeting SDK 36 can no longer opt out of edge-to-edge display; the deprecated Window.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(true)/opt-out APIs are ignored on Android 16. A full-bleed timer with a perimeter progress stroke tracing the real display corners and a cover layout that must keep the bottom-corner camera area clear will draw under the system bars and cutout by default — this must be designed for from the start, not discovered late.
issues.correction: Plan for forced edge-to-edge on targetSdk 36: consume WindowInsets (systemBars, displayCutout) explicitly, drive the perimeter stroke geometry off the rounded-corner/inset/cutout metrics, and pad interactive UI out of the status/nav/cutout regions rather than assuming an inset-fitted window.

issues.claim: Gotchas / Finding 1b: "Handler.postDelayed and most delay()/Thread.sleep timing run on the uptimeMillis clock, which STOPS in deep sleep."
issues.problem: Imprecise. Handler.postDelayed and coroutine delay() on Dispatchers.Main do use SystemClock.uptimeMillis(), but delay() on background dispatchers (Default/IO) is driven by DefaultExecutor using System.nanoTime() (CLOCK_MONOTONIC), not uptimeMillis. The blanket 'uptimeMillis' claim is technically wrong for the dispatcher the timing loop is most likely to run on. Low severity because both clocks freeze in deep sleep, so the actionable conclusion is unaffected.
issues.correction: State it as: neither uptimeMillis (Handler / Main-dispatcher delay) nor nanoTime (background-dispatcher delay) advances during deep sleep, so never accumulate delay deltas — always recompute remaining from elapsedRealtime(). The recompute-from-elapsedRealtime rule is the load-bearing part and is correct.

additions: Wake-lock safety-timeout caveat for the build: the JSON recommends acquire(safetyTimeoutMs) as a crash-safety cap. Make that timeout longer than the longest plausible single workout (or refresh/re-acquire per interval), otherwise the wake lock self-releases mid-workout and screen-off beeps stop — the exact failure the wake lock exists to prevent. Pair it with a guaranteed release() in onDestroy/pause/stop.

collectAsStateWithLifecycle() is not in core Compose — it requires the androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-runtime-compose dependency. Add it to the module's build.gradle so the recommended UI-collection pattern compiles.

Samsung-specific battery management beyond AOSP Doze is correctly flagged in the JSON's gotchas, but for the real build the practical fix on One UI 8 is two settings, not one: request the battery-optimization exemption (ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS) AND have the user add the app to Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > 'Never sleeping apps'. Verify on-device that a multi-minute screen-off rest keeps beeps landing.

research.summary: For a personal, sideloaded Kotlin/Compose interval timer targeting only the newest Android (Android 16 / API 36, which the Galaxy Z Flip 7 ships with), the audio design is: (1) DUCK the user's music by requesting audio focus with AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK via AudioFocusRequest — but acquire it around the whole 5s countdown-beep cluster and release after the 'go' tone, NOT per individual beep (per-beep churn makes the music flutter up/down every second and adds latency). (2) Produce cue tones with pre-rendered enveloped WAV files played through SoundPool as the primary recommendation (least code, predictable, designer-tuned), or synthesized enveloped sines via AudioTrack MODE_STATIC as the no-asset alternative; reject ToneGenerator (harsh DTMF-style tones, poor control). (3) A concrete four-cue palette using musical pitches with raised-cosine envelopes. (4) Audibility over loud music comes mainly from USAGE_ALARM (rides the alarm stream, independent of the media volume the user lowered) plus the ducking; the foreground service must be type 'mediaPlayback' to keep beeping with the screen off, and on Android 15+ audio focus only succeeds while an FGS is running (which we have). (5) Pre-load all samples and schedule cues off a monotonic clock with a small latency lead so the beep lands on the second. Several items (USAGE_ALARM + MAY_DUCK ducking behavior, screen-off timing without a wakelock, exact speaker audibility) are real hardware-tuning knobs that MUST be tested on the physical Z Flip 7.

findings.title: Ducking: request AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK via AudioFocusRequest (API 26+); auto-ducks the music app with no callback
findings.detail: Build an AudioFocusRequest with setFocusGain(AudioManager.AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK) and setAudioAttributes(...), then audioManager.requestAudioFocus(request) / audioManager.abandonAudioFocusRequest(request). When you hold MAY_DUCK focus, the system automatically ducks (lowers) the current focus owner's players — Spotify etc. dip — and the music app does NOT get an onAudioFocusChange callback (the system does the ducking itself). Ducking is triggered by the GAIN type, not by your usage, so you do not implement the volume drop yourself. AudioFocusRequest and requestAudioFocus(AudioFocusRequest) require API 26; the old requestAudioFocus(listener, streamType, durationHint) is deprecated. Because the app targets only Android 16 and runs on one device, set minSdk high (>=26, realistically 34/35) and skip the deprecated legacy-focus branch entirely — no compat code needed.

findings.title: Acquire/release focus around the 5s beep CLUSTER, not per individual beep
findings.detail: The spec's beep window at each interval end is 5s-tone, then 3s/2s/1s beeps, then the 'go' tone at 0 — a ~5-second cluster. Acquiring focus for each ~150ms beep and releasing between them makes the music audibly duck-and-rise every single second (ducking has attack/release ramps of tens of ms), and adds a focus round-trip before each beep. Cleaner and still matches 'duck only while beeping': request focus once when the 5s-tone fires and abandon it right after the 'go' tone (~5s held), which also stays well under the ~15s window Android expects for a TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK holder. Between clusters (mid-interval silence) hold no focus, so the music plays at full volume. Per-beep focus is technically possible if the user insists on literal per-beep ducking, but it sounds worse — flag this tradeoff to the user.

findings.title: Tone production: SoundPool with pre-rendered WAVs (primary) or AudioTrack MODE_STATIC synthesis (alternative); avoid ToneGenerator
findings.detail: SoundPool decodes clips to raw 16-bit PCM in memory once and gives low-latency, repeatable playback with per-play volume/rate control — best fit for four short cues, and the least code: design the tones (with baked-in soft envelope) in an audio editor, ship 4 tiny WAVs in res/raw, load once. AudioTrack MODE_STATIC is the no-asset-files alternative: synthesize each enveloped sine into a short PCM buffer once, keep the AudioTrack instances, and re-trigger with stop()/reloadStaticData()/play(); marginally lower latency but you hand-roll the envelope in code. ToneGenerator should be rejected — it produces harsh, telephony/DTMF-style tones with essentially no envelope or timbre control and a limited fixed tone set. Recommendation: SoundPool + 4 bundled WAVs for predictability and minimal code; only reach for AudioTrack synthesis if you want zero bundled assets.

findings.title: Pleasant tones need a raised-cosine envelope and zero-crossing start/stop
findings.detail: Clicks/pops come from amplitude discontinuities: a non-zero start sample or an abrupt cut. Fix with (a) start the oscillator phase at 0, (b) a short raised-cosine (Hann-like) fade-in of ~5–10 ms, (c) a longer fade-out of ~30–60 ms, (d) end on a zero crossing. Sample formula per sample n: amp * envelope(n) * sin(2*pi*f*n/sampleRate). For a warmer, less sterile beep add a small amount of 2nd/3rd harmonic (e.g. fundamental + ~20% at 2f) rather than a pure sine. Use 44100 Hz, 16-bit PCM, mono. This applies whether you pre-render the WAVs or synthesize via AudioTrack — the envelope is the difference between a 'nice chime' and a 'clicky blip'.

findings.title: Concrete four-cue tone design (pitches + durations)
findings.detail: All with the envelope above. (1) 5-SECONDS warning — distinct mid tone, single note E5 ~659 Hz, ~200 ms, moderate level; clearly lower/rounder than the countdown blips so it reads as 'get ready'. (2) 3s/2s/1s COUNTDOWN — identical short blips, A5 ~880 Hz, ~110–130 ms each, 8 ms attack / 50 ms decay; short and crisp, repeated identically. (3) GO / transition — distinct, brighter and slightly longer: either an upward chirp 880 Hz -> ~1319 Hz over ~300 ms, or a two-note major-third chord C6+E6 (~1047 + 1319 Hz) held ~350 ms at a hair higher level so the transition feels rewarding. Keeping the countdown blips a pure single pitch and making the 5s-tone lower and the go-tone higher/richer gives three unmistakably different sounds. Treat exact Hz/durations as a tuning starting point to refine by ear on the device.

findings.title: Audibility over loud music: use USAGE_ALARM on the beep player; ducking handles the phone's own music
findings.detail: AudioAttributes usage supersedes stream types and drives routing/focus/volume. Give the beep player AudioAttributes usage = USAGE_ALARM (content type CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION) so it rides the alarm volume, which is typically near max and independent of the media volume the user turned down for their music — this is what makes the beep cut through even when the user's own music is loud. The phone's own background music additionally ducks while you hold MAY_DUCK focus. For cut-through against bass-heavy ambient gym sound, note human hearing peaks around 2–4 kHz; the recommended 880 Hz–1.3 kHz cues stay pleasant, and you can add a harmonic partial in the 2–3 kHz band to help them pierce without being shrill. FLAG_AUDIBILITY_ENFORCED exists but is intended for enforced system sounds (e.g. camera shutter) and is not a reliable lever for a normal app — do not depend on it. Do not programmatically override the user's volume; just set the player volume to 1.0.

findings.title: Foreground service: type 'mediaPlayback' keeps beeps working with screen off (API 34+ rules)
findings.detail: Declare android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback" on the <service>, and request both FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK permissions in the manifest; pass the type to startForeground() (required on API 34+). The mediaPlayback type is what lets audio continue when the screen is off / app backgrounded, backed by an ongoing notification. Sideloading (no Play Console) means the Play policy declaration doesn't apply, but the OS still enforces the type + permission at runtime on Android 14+, so you must declare them. This same FGS is what makes audio-focus requests legal on Android 15+ (next finding).

findings.title: Android 15+ (API 35+): audio focus only granted while top app OR running an FGS
findings.detail: On apps targeting Android 15+, requestAudioFocus returns AUDIOFOCUS_REQUEST_FAILED unless the app is the top (visible) app or is running a foreground service. Since the timer runs a mediaPlayback FGS during a workout, the per-cluster focus requests will succeed even with the screen off / app backgrounded. There is an open Google issue (issuetracker 375228130) reporting audio-focus-from-FGS failures on some Android 15 setups — I could not read its contents (sign-in wall), so treat it as a known risk and verify focus is actually granted on the physical Z Flip 7.

findings.title: Pre-loading & landing the beep on the second
findings.detail: SoundPool loads asynchronously — call load() for all 4 cues at workout setup, register setOnLoadCompleteListener, and don't allow Start until every sample reports status==0; otherwise the first play is silently dropped ('sample not ready'). For AudioTrack MODE_STATIC, pre-write the PCM buffers once and keep the instances warm. Audio-API latency for a short beep (tens of ms) is imperceptible for a timer; the real accuracy risk is scheduler jitter. Drive the countdown off a monotonic clock (SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos), compute each cue's absolute target time, and fire a few ms early to compensate for output latency — you can estimate the fast-path buffer from AudioManager.getProperty(PROPERTY_OUTPUT_FRAMES_PER_BUFFER) and PROPERTY_OUTPUT_SAMPLE_RATE. Optionally pre-warm by playing a cue at volume 0 once so the audio HAL is hot on the first real beep.

recommendations: Ducking: create one reusable AudioFocusRequest with setFocusGain(AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK). Acquire it when the 5s warning tone fires at each interval end and abandon it right after the 'go' tone (~5s hold), not per beep. Hold no focus between clusters so music plays full-volume mid-interval.

Tones: ship 4 pre-rendered 44.1kHz/16-bit mono WAVs in res/raw and play via a single SoundPool (load all at workout start, gate Start on OnLoadCompleteListener). This is the least code and most predictable. Only synthesize with AudioTrack MODE_STATIC if you specifically want zero bundled assets.
Do NOT use ToneGenerator — harsh, envelope-less, limited tone set.

Give the SoundPool/AudioTrack AudioAttributes usage = USAGE_ALARM (content type CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION) so beeps ride alarm volume and stay audible over loud music regardless of media volume; set player volume 1.0 and never override the user's system volume.
Bake a raised-cosine envelope into every cue (5-10ms fade-in, 30-60ms fade-out, phase starts at 0, ends on a zero crossing) to kill clicks. Add a small 2nd/3rd-harmonic partial for warmth.

Cue palette to start from and tune by ear: 5s = E5 ~659Hz/200ms (round, lower); 3-2-1 = identical A5 ~880Hz/~120ms blips; GO = brighter/longer, either 880->1319Hz chirp/300ms or a C6+E6 (~1047+1319Hz) chord/350ms.

Foreground service: type mediaPlayback + FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK permissions; pass the type to startForeground(). This keeps beeps firing screen-off and makes Android 15+ audio-focus requests legal.
Because the app targets only Android 16 on one device, set minSdk high (>=34) and skip all deprecated audio-focus / pre-API-26 branches — no compatibility code.
Schedule cues off SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos with absolute target timestamps and a small latency lead; pre-load and pre-warm samples so the first beep isn't dropped or late.
gotchas: MUST verify on the physical Z Flip 7: that USAGE_ALARM + AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK actually DUCKS Spotify (music keeps playing quieter) rather than pausing it. If it misbehaves, fall back to requesting focus with USAGE_MEDIA/USAGE_ASSISTANCE_SONIFICATION while still playing the beep on USAGE_ALARM — but that focus/player usage mismatch is itself unverified and needs a device check.

Screen-off timing: a foreground service does NOT by itself guarantee the CPU stays awake during the ~20-50s of silence between beep clusters; Doze/scheduler throttling can delay a scheduled wake. To guarantee cues land on time with the screen off, hold a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK for the duration of an active workout, or keep a silent/near-silent looping AudioTrack alive to keep the audio path and its wakelock warm. This is a real reliability knob to test, not assume.
SoundPool silently drops play() calls if the sample isn't finished loading ('sample not ready') — you must gate the workout start on OnLoadCompleteListener, or the very first beep won't sound.

Open Google issue 375228130 reports audio-focus-from-FGS failures on some Android 15 configurations; I couldn't read the ticket (auth wall). Confirm focus is granted on-device before relying on ducking.

AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK will NOT duck a focus owner that set CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH or setWillPauseWhenDucked(true) (e.g. a podcast/navigation app) — those pause or are unaffected instead of ducking. Acceptable for this app but worth knowing.
FLAG_AUDIBILITY_ENFORCED is meant for enforced system sounds (camera shutter) and is unreliable for a third-party app — do not use it as the audibility strategy; rely on USAGE_ALARM.
openQuestions: Does the user want literal per-individual-beep ducking (music flutters up/down each second) or per-cluster ducking (music ducks for the ~5s countdown then returns)? Per-cluster is recommended and sounds better; confirm this reading of 'only while the beep sounds' is acceptable.

On the actual Z Flip 7 + One UI 8, does USAGE_ALARM route the beep to both stereo speakers at a level that clearly beats loud ambient gym music, or is a higher-frequency harmonic partial needed? Requires on-device tuning.
Is 'loud gym music' the phone's own music (handled by ducking) or external speakers in the room (only helped by loudness + frequency choice)? Affects how hard to push audibility.
Should the cover-screen (external display) workout keep the same audio path, or is there any risk the small-display MultiStar context changes FGS/audio-focus behavior? Worth a quick device check.

confirmedHighlights: HARDWARE CORRECT: Galaxy Z Flip 7 shipped July 2025 running One UI 8 / Android 16 out of the box, and Android 16 = API level 36. Confirmed via Samsung Global Newsroom and SamMobile.

SDK GATE CORRECT: AudioFocusRequest and requestAudioFocus(AudioFocusRequest)/abandonAudioFocusRequest(AudioFocusRequest) require API 26 (Android 8.0); the old requestAudioFocus(listener, streamType, durationHint) is deprecated. Correctly avoided the deprecated legacy branch. Source: developer.android.com/media/optimize/audio-focus.

SDK GATE CORRECT: Android 15 (API 35) restricts audio focus to the top app OR an app running a foreground service, returning AUDIOFOCUS_REQUEST_FAILED otherwise. Verified in behavior-changes-15. The docs do NOT require a specific FGS type, so the workout's mediaPlayback FGS satisfies the exemption (the research's claim is right).

DUCKING MECHANICS CORRECT: With AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK the system auto-ducks the focus owner without invoking its onAudioFocusChange() callback (since API 26); an app opts into pause-instead-of-duck via setWillPauseWhenDucked(true) + OnAudioFocusChangeListener. The gotcha that CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH / setWillPauseWhenDucked apps pause instead of duck is accurate. Verified verbatim on the audio-focus doc.

FGS TYPE CORRECT: mediaPlayback requires the FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK permission (plus FOREGROUND_SERVICE) and has 'Runtime prerequisites: None' (no MediaSession needed). startForegroundServiceType enforcement is Android 14 (API 34). Verified on fgs/service-types.

AUDIO ATTRIBUTES CORRECT: USAGE_ALARM (rides STREAM_ALARM, independent of media volume) + CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION are the right constants, and rejecting FLAG_AUDIBILITY_ENFORCED (documented as a legacy STREAM_SYSTEM_ENFORCED / camera-shutter lever, unreliable for third-party apps) is correct. Verified on source.android.com/docs/core/audio/attributes.
The cited open Google issue 375228130 ('Android 15 - Request Audio Focus not working for Foreground service') is a real tracker item; treating it as a device-verification risk is appropriate.

No hallucinated or misnamed APIs found: SoundPool.OnLoadCompleteListener/setOnLoadCompleteListener, AudioTrack MODE_STATIC + reloadStaticData(), AudioManager.PROPERTY_OUTPUT_FRAMES_PER_BUFFER / PROPERTY_OUTPUT_SAMPLE_RATE, SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos are all real. The tone pitches map correctly to E5=659, A5=880, C6=1047, E6=1319 Hz. Rejecting ToneGenerator and all pre-API-26 compat is the right call for a newest-Android-only single-device build.

issues.claim: Foreground service: declare android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback" and request both FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK permissions in the manifest.
issues.problem: IMPORTANT OMISSION: the manifest permission list leaves out POST_NOTIFICATIONS, and the research never mentions the runtime notification grant. An FGS must post an ongoing notification; on Android 13+ (API 33) that notification is silently suppressed unless the app holds the runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission. On a device that ships Android 16 (the Z Flip 7's exact case) the user would run a workout with no visible timer notification, and One UI can flag/limit an FGS whose notification never appears. This is a real build gap, not a policy nicety.
issues.correction: Also declare <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"/> and request it at runtime (API 33+) before the first workout, then build the FGS's ongoing notification. Handle the denied case (FGS still runs, but warn the user their timer notification is hidden).

issues.claim: Request focus once when the 5s-tone fires and abandon it right after the 'go' tone (~5s held) ... this 'still matches duck only while beeping'.
issues.problem: SPEC DEVIATION (disclosed but understated): the fixed spec says beeps 'duck the user's background music ONLY while the beep sounds, then music returns.' Holding MAY_DUCK focus across the whole ~5s cluster keeps the music ducked during the silent gaps too — nothing plays at 4s, and there are ~1s gaps between the 3/2/1 blips and before 'go' — so the music stays down for ~5 continuous seconds, not only while a tone is audible. The research raises this as an open question (good), but the 'still matches' framing overstates the fit: it is a deliberate deviation from the literal spec, not a match.
issues.correction: Flag it to the user as a deviation and get sign-off. If literal per-beep ducking is required, acquire/release focus per beep (accept the flutter) or gate ducking to each tone's actual duration; per-cluster is the better-sounding default but must be an explicit choice, not presented as spec-compliant.

issues.claim: The mediaPlayback type is what lets audio continue when the screen is off / app backgrounded ... the FGS must be type 'mediaPlayback' to keep beeping with the screen off.
issues.problem: IMPRECISE CAUSATION (minor): mediaPlayback is the correct type to DECLARE for an ongoing-audio use case and is required to run the FGS legally on API 34+, but the type itself is not what keeps audio playing or timing accurate with the screen off. Audio continues because an active audio session + foregrounded process, and the research's own gotcha correctly notes a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK (or a warm silent AudioTrack) is what actually guarantees the CPU wakes to fire cues during the ~20-50s silent gaps. The summary phrasing implies the FGS type alone delivers screen-off reliability, which it does not.
issues.correction: Declare mediaPlayback (correct type), but rely on the active audio path + a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK held for the duration of an active workout for screen-off timing accuracy — treat the wakelock as required, not optional, and verify on-device.

additions: USAGE_ALARM routes to STREAM_ALARM, which on most builds also plays through Do Not Disturb — desirable here (beeps sound even in DnD), but worth knowing it's a behavior change vs USAGE_MEDIA. Crucially, audibility then depends on the user's ALARM volume, which is NOT guaranteed 'near max' as the research assumes; it's a separate slider the user may have lowered. For a real build, surface an in-app check/prompt if AudioManager.getStreamVolume(STREAM_ALARM) is low, since the app is told never to override system volume.

If the AudioTrack MODE_STATIC path is chosen for lowest latency, add AudioTrack.Builder.setPerformanceMode(AudioTrack.PERFORMANCE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY) (API 26+) — the research discusses latency and a pre-warm play at volume 0 but omits this explicit low-latency request. Minor: latency is imperceptible for a timer, so this is optional polish, not a fix.
SoundPool has a per-sample decoded-size ceiling (~1 MB); the four short enveloped cues are far under it, so this is fine, but keep the WAVs short (the design already implies this).

The USAGE_ALARM-on-player + MAY_DUCK-on-focus-request combination is sound in theory (ducking is driven by the incoming focus GAIN type, not by the requester's player usage), so it should duck Spotify — the research's own gotcha to device-verify this on the Z Flip 7 is the right call and should not be dropped.

languages.name: Mandarin Chinese

numberWords.compositionRule: Han place-value. Tens = [digit 2-5] + 十 (二十=20, 三十=30, 四十=40, 五十=50). 21-59 = [tens digit 2-5]十[ones 1-9]; exact tens drop the ones (三十 = 30). Seconds under 10 are the bare digit word (五 = 5). IMPORTANT: the number-WORD for zero is 零 (U+96F6); the digit-SLOT zero glyph for a fixed-width clock is 〇 (U+3007) — different characters. Use 二 (èr) for the numeral 2, never 两 (liǎng, which is only 'two of something').

languages.clockRendering: Two options for the big MM:SS. (A) Place-value Han e.g. 12:34 -> 十二:三十四: reads as proper words ('twelve : thirty-four') but is VARIABLE-WIDTH (三十四 is 3 glyphs for a 2-digit field vs 五 for :05), so the clock jitters and the two sides of the colon never align — poor for a large clock, and 十二:三十四 no longer reads as a clock face. (B) Digit-by-digit Han e.g. 12:34 -> 一二:三四, with 〇 (U+3007) for zero so 05:09 -> 〇五:〇九: fixed two-glyph fields, full-width glyphs align perfectly across the colon, and it looks maximally exotic to a bystander. Its only cost: a native reader parses 三四 as 'three four' (phone-number style) rather than 'thirty-four', but it is still legible position-by-position. RECOMMEND option B (digit-by-digit Han with 〇 for zero) for the large clock; reserve place-value composition (三十四) for the optional word-mode readout under a minute, where reading it as a word is the whole point. Use a full-width colon ：(U+FF1A) so the separator matches the full-width glyph metrics. Pitfalls: never mix place-value on one side and digits on the other; use 〇 not 零 or ASCII 0 in the digit clock; bundle a CJK font (Noto Sans/Serif CJK SC) since system fallback may substitute a wrong glyph for 〇.
languages.notes: LTR; no letter case; no cursive joining or contextual shaping. Han numerals are full-width and metrically uniform — ideal for a monospaced clock. Critical distinction: 〇 (U+3007, digit-position zero, numeric value 0) vs 零 (U+96F6, the spoken number word). Labels shown are Simplified; Traditional is 運動 / 休息 (休息 unchanged). Verified glyphs: 〇 U+3007, 一 U+4E00, 二 U+4E8C, 三 U+4E09, 四 U+56DB, 五 U+4E94, 六 U+516D, 七 U+4E03, 八 U+516B, 九 U+4E5D, 十 U+5341.

languages.name: Japanese

numberWords.compositionRule: Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) place-value, glyphs identical to Chinese Han numerals: [tens 2-5]十[ones 1-9]. 十 jū=10, 二十 nijū=20, 三十 sanjū=30, 四十 yonjū=40, 五十 gojū=50. Readings: 21 nijūichi, 34 sanjūyon, 45 yonjūgo, 59 gojūkyū. The written glyph is invariant even where readings vary (4=yon/shi, 7=nana/shichi, 9=kyū/ku) — irrelevant here since the feature is visual with no audio. Word-zero is 零 (rei); digit-slot zero is 〇 (U+3007). This is the number system Japanese uses for counting minutes (分) and seconds (秒).

languages.clockRendering: Same digit-by-digit vs place-value tradeoff as Chinese (shared glyphs). Everyday Japanese digital clocks use Western Arabic digits, so a kanji-numeral clock reads as deliberately archaic/stylized — which serves the 'intrigue' goal well. RECOMMEND digit-by-digit Sino-Japanese kanji with 〇 (U+3007) for zero for the fixed-width clock (05:34 -> 〇五:三四), aligned and exotic; use place-value composition (三十四) only for the optional word-mode readout under a minute. Pitfall: stacked kanji numerals feel unusual to Japanese readers in a horizontal digital layout (they associate kanji numerals with vertical writing) — acceptable for a stylized timer but worth knowing. Use a full-width colon ：(U+FF1A). Bundle Noto Sans CJK JP.
languages.notes: LTR; no case; no joining/shaping. Numeral glyphs are the same code points as Chinese Han numerals but this is the Sino-Japanese reading set (the one used for 分/秒). 〇 (U+3007) = digit-slot zero; 零 = the word. Full-width and metrically uniform, aligns cleanly. Note: some shared kanji differ subtly between Noto CJK JP and CJK SC regional variants, but the numerals 〇一二三四五六七八九十 are visually equivalent across both — either font is safe for this feature. No RTL. Alternate label option: トレーニング / 休憩 (katakana 'training'), but 運動 / 休憩 is shorter and cleaner.

languages.name: Korean
languages.script: Hangul (Sino-Korean numerals; no native numeral glyphs)

numberWords.compositionRule: SINO-KOREAN place-value, syllable blocks concatenated with NO space: [tens 이/삼/사/오]+[십]+[ones 일-구]. 십=10, 이십=20, 삼십=30, 사십=40, 오십=50. 21->이십일, 34->삼십사, 45->사십오, 59->오십구. Seconds under 10 = bare digit word (오 = 5). Zero = 영 (use 공 only when reading a raw digit string, e.g. phone numbers). CRITICAL: minutes (분) and seconds (초) REQUIRE the Sino-Korean set given here; native Korean numbers (하나 둘 셋 …) are used only for hours (시) and counting reps — do NOT use them for the seconds/minutes countdown.

languages.clockRendering: Korean has NO native numeral glyphs, and every real Korean digital clock/countdown uses Western Arabic digits. RECOMMEND: keep Western digits for the large MM:SS clock. To get the 'can't read it' effect, use word mode — spell the seconds in Sino-Korean Hangul when under a minute (34 -> 삼십사) with a small Western-digit fallback clock. Do NOT try to render a spelled Hangul clock full-time: syllable blocks are variable-width so MM:SS won't align, and it reads awkwardly. Hard pitfall: seconds/minutes take Sino-Korean, so never display native Korean (하나 둘 셋 …) for the countdown — that is grammatically wrong for 초/분. Zero in a spelled countdown is 영.
languages.notes: LTR; no case; no joining/shaping. usesNativeDigits=false because Hangul has no dedicated numeral symbols — numbers are written as Western digits or spelled as syllable blocks. TWO number systems exist and the distinction matters here: Sino-Korean (일 이 삼 … , provided above) is correct for minutes/seconds; native Korean (하나 둘 셋 넷 다섯 …; tens 스물/서른/마흔/쉰) is for hours and counting objects/reps and must NOT be used for the timer's seconds. 육 (6) / 십육 (16) undergo pronunciation sandhi but spelling is stable — moot with no audio. Zero: 영 (general/countdown) vs 공 (reading digit strings aloud). Hangul syllable blocks are near-uniform width but not full-width monospace like CJK ideographs.

corrections.given: Hangul syllable blocks are 'variable-width' / 'near-uniform width but not full-width monospace like CJK ideographs' — used to justify not rendering a spelled MM:SS clock
corrections.correct: Each Hangul syllable is Unicode East Asian Width = Wide (full-width, uniform per block), the SAME width class as CJK ideographs. A spelled MM:SS fails to align not because individual blocks vary in width but because the NUMBER of syllable blocks varies per number (오 = 1 block vs 삼십사 = 3 blocks). The recommendation itself (keep Western digits for the large clock, spell Sino-Korean only in word mode) remains sound; only the stated width justification is inaccurate.

languages.name: Hindi

numberWords.compositionRule: NO algorithmic composition — Hindi 1–99 is highly irregular; nearly every value is a distinct memorized word with heavy Sanskrit-derived sandhi (e.g. 21 इक्कीस = ek+bīs but fused unpredictably). You MUST ship a hard-coded lookup table for 0–59; do not build 'tens-word + unit-word'. The only reliable sub-pattern: values ending in 9 use an 'un-' (one-less-than-next-ten) prefix — 19 उन्नीस, 29 उनतीस, 39 उनतालीस, 49 उनचास, 59 उनसठ (built off the FOLLOWING ten). For the timer's 0–59 second/minute range, a 60-entry table is the correct approach.

languages.clockRendering: Use native Devanagari digits ०–९ for the large MM:SS clock — they maximize the 'intriguing, unreadable to a bystander' effect and are historically correct for Hindi. (Note: modern digital India frequently uses Western 0–9 on clocks, so native digits read as deliberately exotic, which is exactly the goal.) Digits are fixed-width and left-to-right; a standard ':' separator works. Pitfall: ensure the render font actually carries Devanagari digit glyphs (Noto Sans Devanagari or the Android system font both do); a Latin-only font will tofu them. For word-mode under 60s, drive from the lookup table, not composition.
languages.notes: LTR script, no letter case. Devanagari digits are U+0966–U+096F. Isolated digits need no shaping, but the WORD forms require a Devanagari shaping engine (HarfBuzz — built into Android since early versions) for conjuncts and vowel signs: क्क in इक्कीस, न्द्र in पंद्रह, त्र in सत्रह. Do NOT drop the chandrabindu — 5 is पाँच (chandrabindu ँ); the anusvara form पांच is a common digital variant but पाँच is dictionary-correct. 6 छह also appears as छः. Work=काम (kām, 'work'); Rest=आराम (ārām, 'rest') — for a fitness break; विश्राम (vishrām) is a more formal alternative for 'rest'. Spot-checks verified against Wiktionary (इक्कीस=21, चौंतीस=34, पैंतालीस=45, उनसठ=59) and Omniglot; 0–20 and tens verified against Omniglot.

languages.name: Bengali

numberWords.compositionRule: NO algorithmic composition — like Hindi, Bengali 1–99 is highly irregular; each value is a distinct memorized word (21 একুশ, 34 চৌত্রিশ). Ship a hard-coded 0–59 lookup table; do not concatenate tens+units. Sub-pattern: values ending in 9 take the classical 'ūn-' (one-less) prefix built off the NEXT ten — 19 উনিশ, 29 ঊনত্রিশ, 39 ঊনচল্লিশ, 49 ঊনপঞ্চাশ, 59 ঊনষাট. A 60-entry table covers the timer's 0–59 range correctly.

languages.clockRendering: Use native Bengali digits ০–৯ for the large MM:SS clock. They are strongly exotic to a Latin-reading bystander — and helpfully so: ৪ (4) looks like a Western 8 and ৭ (7)/৮ (8) are easily misread, which reinforces the 'can't read it' intrigue. Fixed-width, left-to-right, standard ':' separator. Pitfall: use a font with Bengali digits (Noto Sans Bengali or Android system font). Word-mode strings under 60s come from the lookup table.
languages.notes: LTR, no case. Bengali digits are U+09E6–U+09EF. WORD forms need Bengali complex shaping (native on Android) for conjuncts and vowel signs: ল্ল in চল্লিশ/পঁয়তাল্লিশ, ঞ্চ in পঞ্চাশ, ত্র in ত্রিশ/চৌত্রিশ. Preserve the chandrabindu ঁ (পাঁচ, পঁয়তাল্লিশ) and the য় (ya-phalaka/ya with nukta) in ছয়/নয়/পঁয়তাল্লিশ. Spelling variation to be aware of: the classical 'less-by-one' prefix ঊন (long ঊ, U+098A) vs colloquial উন (short উ, U+0989) — 19 is conventionally short উনিশ, while 59 is given here as ঊনষাট per Omniglot/etymology (উনষাট also circulates). 0 শূন্য uses long ূ (U+09C2); some casual sources write শুন্য. 16 ষোলো also appears as ষোল. Work=কাজ (kaj, 'work'); Rest=বিশ্রাম (bishram, 'rest/break') — the natural fitness term; আরাম (aram) means 'comfort/ease', less apt for a rest interval. Spot-checks verified against Wiktionary (একুশ=21, চৌত্রিশ=34, পঁয়তাল্লিশ=45) and Omniglot (ঊনষাট=59); 0–20 and tens verified against Omniglot.

languages.name: Thai

numberWords.compositionRule: FULLY regular decimal — you can compose algorithmically. Tens = [unit word] + สิบ (sìp, 'ten'), then append the unit word for 1–9. Two exceptions: (1) the tens word for 20 is ยี่สิบ (yîi-sìp), NOT สองสิบ; 10 alone is just สิบ (no หนึ่ง prefix). (2) a TRAILING 1 becomes เอ็ด (èt), not หนึ่ง — so 21 = ยี่สิบเอ็ด, 31 = สามสิบเอ็ด, 41 = สี่สิบเอ็ด. Everything 22–59 (except x1) is simply tens-word + unit-word with no spaces. Examples: 34 สามสิบสี่, 45 สี่สิบห้า, 59 ห้าสิบเก้า.

spotChecks.word: ยี่สิบเอ็ด
ห้าสิบเก้า

languages.clockRendering: Native Thai digits ๐–๙ on the large MM:SS clock give maximum bystander intrigue (in modern Thailand Western 0–9 dominate on clocks, so Thai numerals read as deliberately unusual). They are fixed-width and left-to-right; standard ':' works. Alternatively keep Western digits if you want it to still feel like a normal clock and reserve the exotic effect for word-mode. Pitfall: use a Thai-capable font (Noto Sans Thai / Android system). In WORD mode, Thai is written with NO spaces between words (ห้าสิบเก้า is one run) — do not insert spaces or the reading looks broken.
languages.notes: LTR, no letter case, no inter-word spaces. Thai digits are U+0E50–U+0E59. Word forms use pre-base vowels and stacked tone/vowel marks that need Thai shaping (native on Android): เ in เจ็ด/เอ็ด/เก้า is a LEADING vowel — store text in logical (typed) order and let the shaper render เ before its consonant; do not manually reorder. Also present: ็ (mai taikhu) in เอ็ด/เจ็ด, and tone marks ่/้ in สี่/ห้า/เก้า — keep them attached. Avoid inserting ZWSP inside a number word. Work=ทำงาน (tham-ngaan, 'to work') — natural but a touch long; งาน alone ('work') is a shorter option. Rest=พัก (phák, 'to rest/take a break') — the standard, short fitness term. All digits and number words verified against the Wikipedia 'Thai numerals' article (including the ยี่สิบ=20 and terminal เอ็ด=1 rules).

languages.name: Arabic

numberWords.compositionRule: For 21-59: [unit word] + [tens word], with the unit FIRST (reverse of English) and joined by the conjunction وَ ('wa' = and), which is written attached to the front of the tens word with no space. Pattern: '<unit> و<tens>'. E.g. 34 = أربعة وثلاثون ('four and thirty'), 45 = خمسة وأربعون. The tens word never changes for gender. Because the timer shows bare, noun-less numbers, keep the units in their abstract citation forms (3-9 keep the ة ending: ثلاثة، أربعة، خمسة …); do NOT apply the reverse-polarity noun agreement. Transliteration model: waahid wa-'ishruun (21), arba'a wa-thalaathuun (34), khamsa wa-arba'uun (45), tis'a wa-khamsuun (59).

languages.clockRendering: Use the native Arabic-Indic digit glyphs (٠-٩) for the big MM:SS clock — that is the authentic, intriguing look and is fully natural to Arabic readers. Digits WITHIN a two-digit group already run left-to-right (tens digit on the left, units on the right), identical to Western order — do NOT reverse them. Render minutes on the LEFT, colon, seconds on the RIGHT: e.g. 2:45 -> ٠٢:٤٥. PITFALL (bidi): Arabic-Indic digits are Unicode bidi class AN and the colon is a neutral/weak separator; in an RTL paragraph the whole 'AN : AN' run can MIRROR so minutes end up on the right and seconds on the left. Fix: force the clock element to LTR. In Compose either (a) lay MM, ':', SS out as separate Text runs inside an explicit left-to-right Row (LayoutDirection.Ltr), or (b) set the clock TextStyle textDirection = TextDirection.Ltr / wrap with LRM U+200E or an LTR isolate LRI U+2066 … PDI U+2069. Use a plain colon U+003A. WORD MODE (under a minute): spell the seconds in Arabic, which is ordinary RTL text and needs no special handling — e.g. 45 -> خمسة وأربعون, rendered right-to-left; keep the small numeric MM:SS (LTR, per above) as the fallback read beneath it.
languages.notes: RTL + cursive shaping: Arabic runs right-to-left and letters join, changing shape by position (isolated/initial/medial/final). Android/Compose shape automatically via HarfBuzz from the plain Unicode string — never hardcode Arabic Presentation Forms (U+FB50-U+FEFF) and never manually reverse strings. FONT: verify the chosen typeface actually contains Arabic-Indic digit glyphs U+0660-U+0669 AND full Arabic letter shaping (e.g. Noto Naskh Arabic / Noto Sans Arabic); a Latin-only display font picked for the big numbers will tofu or mis-fall-back. Note the U+0664/0665/0666 (4/5/6) glyphs render in the font's regional style — the Mashriqi 'Arabic-Indic' shapes we want, distinct from the Persian/Urdu Extended forms (U+06F0+); pick an Arabic (not Persian) font. LABELS: تمرين (tamriin, 'exercise/work') and راحة (raaha, 'rest') are single RTL words as Arabic fitness apps display them (عمل 'amal, literal 'work', is an acceptable alt for the work label). Center them — centered alignment sidesteps left/right concerns; if edge-aligned, align RIGHT and set the label node's layoutDirection = Rtl. Since the rest of the UI is LTR English, put each Arabic label in its own RTL (or dir=auto) text node so surrounding LTR chrome doesn't drag it. NO CASING: Arabic has no upper/lowercase — don't call toUpperCase() for a 'label' look; it's a no-op. GENDER/AGREEMENT: numbers 3-10 normally take REVERSE polarity agreement with a counted noun; the timer shows numbers with NO noun, so use the abstract citation forms above and apply no agreement. If you ever attach ثانية ('second', feminine) the unit forms would flip — keep the numbers noun-less. CASE ENDINGS: tens have nominative -ون (عشرون) vs oblique -ين (عشرين); '2' has nominative اثنان vs oblique اثنين — use the nominative -ون / اثنان citation forms for standalone display (colloquial speech often uses -ين, but -ون is the MSA citation form). Digits verified against Unicode block Arabic (U+0660-0669); number words/composition verified against multiple MSA counting references.

corrections.given: Claims the whole 'AN : AN' run can MIRROR in an RTL paragraph so minutes end up on the right and seconds on the left, requiring a forced-LTR fix.
corrections.correct: Overstated for a single-string MM:SS with a plain colon. Colon U+003A is bidi class CS and the Arabic-Indic digits are AN; per Unicode UAX #9 rule W4 a single CS between two numbers of the same type is coerced to that type (AN CS AN -> AN AN AN), so '٠٢:٤٥' resolves to one all-AN run that displays LTR with minutes on the left and does NOT mirror by default. Real mirroring only occurs if MM, ':' and SS are separate Compose Text nodes inside an RTL-direction Row; the recommended explicit-Ltr Row / textDirection=Ltr fix is correct and strictly necessary only in that multi-node case (harmless defensive insurance for the single-string case). All other clockRendering guidance (native Arabic-Indic digits, don't reverse within a group, minutes-left, plain colon, RTL word-mode) is sound.
corrections.source: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/ (UAX #9 Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm, rule W4)

languages.name: English

numberWords.compositionRule: tens[20,30,40,50]. For 21-59: tens word + hyphen + unit word (e.g. thirty + '-' + two = thirty-two). All of 21-29, 31-39, 41-49, 51-59 are hyphenated. Watch the spelling of 'forty' (NO 'u', unlike 'four/fourteen').

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (e.g. 04:30 / 00:05). This is the reference/fallback rendering; drop the leading minute zero only if you deliberately want a stopwatch look (4:30). No pitfalls.
languages.notes: LTR, no shaping, no accents. Baseline language for the feature; the clock stays plain digits and the 'word mode' (spelled-out seconds under a minute) is the visual gimmick. Common short label alternatives a fitness app uses: WORK/REST (chosen), or GO/REST, or ON/OFF.

languages.name: Russian

numberWords.compositionRule: tens = 20=двадцать, 30=тридцать, 40=сорок (irregular), 50=пятьдесят. For 21-59: tens word + SPACE + unit word, two separate words, no hyphen (e.g. тридцать + ' ' + четыре = тридцать четыре). Units reuse the 1-9 forms from zeroToTwenty.

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (04:30). Russian natively writes numerals with Western Arabic digits, so this reads instantly and is the right choice; do NOT spell the clock. Pitfall: a fully spelled MM:SS would be awkward because Russian numerals inflect for case — reserve spelled words for the big under-a-minute display only.
languages.notes: Cyrillic, LTR, no shaping. CASE/GENDER caveat for the spelled seconds: Russian '1' and '2' inflect for gender. Use the DEFAULT MASCULINE bare-counting forms: 1=один (not fem. одна), 2=два (not fem. две — a common auto-source error). These are correct for an abstract countdown with no noun shown. If you ever paired the number with the feminine noun секунда it would become одна/две секунды, but since no noun is displayed, один/два is correct and unambiguous. Note double-н in одиннадцать (11). Labels: Работа (Work) / Отдых (Rest); all-caps РАБОТА/ОТДЫХ renders cleanly. Alternative work label: Нагрузка (load), but Работа is the standard Tabata-app term.

languages.name: Spanish

numberWords.compositionRule: tens = 20=veinte, 30=treinta, 40=cuarenta, 50=cincuenta. Two regimes: 21-29 are SINGLE fused words: veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, veinticuatro, veinticinco, veintiséis, veintisiete, veintiocho, veintinueve (accents on veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis). 31-59 are THREE words: tens + 'y' + unit (treinta y cuatro). Do not fuse the thirties/forties/fifties and do not put 'y' inside the twenties.

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (04:30). Spanish uses Western Arabic digits natively. Pitfall: preserve the accents in the spelled word mode (dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis) — a missing accent is a spelling error and undercuts the 'looks authentic' goal.
languages.notes: LTR, no shaping. Accents are mandatory: dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis. '1' is uno in a bare count; it apocopates to 'un' before a masculine noun / 'una' before feminine (and veintiuno→veintiún/veintiuna), but with no noun on screen, uno/veintiuno is correct. In ALL-CAPS keep the accents (RAE recommends DIECISÉIS, not DIECISEIS). Distinct from Portuguese (dos/tres/seis vs dois/três/seis; fused twenties vs Portuguese 'vinte e um'). Alt fitness labels: Activo/Descanso or Esfuerzo/Descanso; Trabajo/Descanso chosen for clarity.

languages.name: French

numberWords.compositionRule: tens = 20=vingt, 30=trente, 40=quarante, 50=cinquante. 21/31/41/51 use 'et un': TRADITIONAL spelling is three words with spaces and no hyphens (vingt et un, trente et un, quarante et un, cinquante et un); the 1990 rectified spelling allows fully-hyphenated vingt-et-un etc. — both correct, pick ONE and stay consistent. All OTHER compounds 22-29,32-39,42-49,52-59 are hyphenated tens-unit (vingt-deux, trente-quatre, quarante-cinq, cinquante-neuf). 17/18/19 are already hyphenated (dix-sept, dix-huit, dix-neuf).

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (04:30). French uses Western Arabic digits. Pitfall: for a seconds stopwatch use the COLON, not the French time conventions 'h'/'min' (4h30 is wall-clock hours:minutes, wrong here). Keep the accent on zéro if a spelled 0 ever appears.
languages.notes: LTR, no shaping. Chosen 21 form is the traditional 'vingt et un' (matches spec); if you prefer the 1990 reform switch every X1 to hyphens (vingt-et-un) and be consistent. Accent on zéro. All-caps renders fine (accents optional on French capitals but keep them for style). Work label: 'Effort' is the idiomatic HIIT term; 'Travail' (literal 'work') also fine. Rest = Repos. Distinct from other Romance langs (quatre/cinq vs cuatro/cinco).

languages.name: German

numberWords.compositionRule: tens = 20=zwanzig, 30=dreißig (ß!), 40=vierzig, 50=fünfzig. For 21-59: unit + 'und' + tens, written as ONE joined word in REVERSED order — literally 'one-and-twenty' (einundzwanzig). Spelling traps: '1' loses its -s inside compounds → 'ein' not 'eins' (einundzwanzig, NOT einsundzwanzig); '6' is sech- (sechzehn/sechzig, dropped -s); '7' is sieb- (siebzehn/siebzig, dropped -en); 30 is dreißig with -ßig eszett so the thirties are e.g. vierunddreißig. Examples: fünfundvierzig (45), neunundfünfzig (59).

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (04:30). German writes clock/stopwatch times with a colon, so this is natural. Pitfall: none for digits — but if you render the spelled word mode in ALL CAPS, the ß in dreißig-based thirties must map to 'SS' (DREISSIG) or the capital ẞ U+1E9E; a naïve uppercase of 'ß' can render wrong.
languages.notes: LTR, no shaping. Umlauts (ü in fünf/fünfzehn/fünfzig, ö in zwölf) and ß (dreißig) are essential glyphs — verify the font ships them. Number words are lowercase (not nouns), so no capitalization needed in word mode. The reversed unit-first order (ein-und-zwanzig) is the big visual surprise for bystanders. Labels: 'Aktiv'/'Pause' is clean and short; 'Belastung' (exertion)/'Pause' is the more literal gym term but long. 'Pause' is a noun → capital P.

languages.name: Portuguese

numberWords.compositionRule: tens = 20=vinte, 30=trinta, 40=quarenta, 50=cinquenta. For 21-59: tens + 'e' + unit, THREE separate words, in EVERY decade with no fusion (vinte e um, trinta e quatro, quarenta e cinco, cinquenta e nove). Key contrast with Spanish, which fuses the twenties (veintiuno) — Portuguese never does. Consistent across European and Brazilian Portuguese.

languages.clockRendering: Keep Western digits, MM:SS with a colon (04:30). Portuguese uses Western Arabic digits. Pitfall: preserve the circumflex on 'três' in word mode; no accent on dezesseis/dezessete.
languages.notes: LTR, no shaping. VARIETY CHOICE: values above are Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR): 16/17/19 = dezesseis/dezessete/dezenove. European Portuguese (PT-PT) uses the deza- link vowel: dezasseis/dezassete/dezanove — swap these three for EP. 14=catorze (valid in BOTH; quatorze is an accepted PT-BR variant). 18=dezoito (both). Accent: três (circumflex). DISTINCT FROM SPANISH: dois vs dos, três vs tres, sete vs siete, nove vs nueve, and 'e' throughout vs Spanish 'y' + fused twenties. Labels: Trabalho/Descanso (works in PT-BR and PT-PT); alt Ativo/Descanso.
